scenario.title: Lancashire Care NHS Foundation Trust v Lancashire County Council
scenario.description: The two claimant NHS Foundation Trusts challenged the award of a £104 million contract for Public Health Nursing and the 0-19 Healthy Child Programme, alleging that the Council's evaluation and scoring was flawed due to inadequate reasons given for the scores awarded. The core allegation is not that a specific calculation was wrong, but that the contracting authority failed to discharge its duty to give sufficiently clear reasons for its evaluation decision.
scenario.bidder_name: Lancashire Care NHS Foundation Trust & Blackpool Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

interests: Compliance & Legality: Ensure the evaluation process was lawful and within our powers under the Procurement Act 2023
Protection of Public Funds: Avoid delays that increase costs, particularly for a £104 million contract with critical public health services at stake
Continuity of Service / Delivery: Deliver essential Public Health Nursing and Healthy Child Programme services to vulnerable populations without interruption
goals: Defend the procurement decision as lawful and rational
Provide sufficient transparency and justification for evaluation scores
ca_pre_negotiation.batna: Defend the decision in the TCC — costly (£50k+) and slow (6-12 months), with a real risk of automatic suspension.
ca_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We stand by our evaluation process, which was transparent and followed published criteria. We are willing to provide additional feedback and clarification on scoring decisions.

interests: Commercial Loss & Recovery: We have already invested £500k in bid costs, and stand to lose a significant share of the £104 million contract value if we don't succeed.

Fairness & Transparency: The Council's failure to provide clear reasons for their evaluation decision undermines our trust in the procurement process and may indicate a deeper issue with transparency in future bids.
Protection of Reputation: A loss due to perceived flaws in the evaluation process could damage our reputation as a reliable bidder, impacting our ability to secure future contracts.
goals: Force a re-evaluation of submitted bids
bidder_pre_negotiation.batna: Pursue a damages claim in the TCC — costly (£50k-£100k in legal fees) for a business our size, slow, and the outcome is uncertain.
bidder_pre_negotiation.opening_position: We request that the Council provides clear reasons for their evaluation decision and re-evaluates our bid to ensure fairness and transparency in the procurement process.

messages.message: I acknowledge that the claimants have raised concerns regarding the transparency of our evaluation process. To clarify, can you specify which particular scores or reasons for scoring are alleged to be inadequate? Furthermore, I would like to offer additional information on our evaluation methodology and provide a detailed breakdown of how we applied the published criteria in this procurement. This may help address some of the claimants' concerns.

Thank you for your offer to provide additional information on your evaluation methodology and a detailed breakdown of how you applied the published criteria in this procurement. I would like to request that you provide this information specifically related to the scoring of our bid, as well as any relevant evaluator comments or feedback. Can you also confirm whether these documents will be made available to us prior to our next meeting?

We will provide the requested information on our evaluation methodology and a detailed breakdown of how we applied the published criteria in this procurement, specifically related to the scoring of your bid. This document will be made available to you prior to our next meeting. We will also include any relevant evaluator comments or feedback that were provided during the evaluation process.
messages.proposal: A voluntary standstill extension for an additional two weeks to allow for further review and discussion
messages.concession_made: We will provide a more detailed breakdown of the scoring, including the specific weightings applied to each criterion

messages.message: Thank you for agreeing to provide additional information on your evaluation methodology and a detailed breakdown of how you applied the published criteria in this procurement, specifically related to the scoring of our bid. We appreciate your willingness to increase transparency. However, we must emphasize that our primary concern remains the lack of clear reasons provided for the scores awarded. In light of this, we would like to propose an independent review of the evaluation process by a neutral third-party expert, who can assess whether the contracting authority's decision-making was fair and transparent. This would not only address our concerns but also provide assurance that the procurement process has been conducted in accordance with best practices.
messages.proposal: An independent review of the evaluation process by a neutral third-party expert

messages.message: We understand your concerns about the lack of clear reasons provided for the scores awarded and are willing to consider an independent review of our evaluation process by a neutral third-party expert. However, we would like to propose a compromise: instead of an external review, we could provide additional training to our evaluators on providing clear and transparent scoring reasons, as well as revising our procurement documentation to include more detailed guidance on this aspect.
messages.proposal: Independent Review of Evaluation Process by Neutral Third-Party Expert

messages.message: We appreciate your willingness to consider our proposal for an independent review by a neutral third-party expert. However, we are concerned that additional training for evaluators and revising procurement documentation may not be sufficient to address our concerns about the lack of clear reasons provided for the scores awarded. We would like to propose a compromise: instead of relying solely on internal measures, why not consider engaging an independent reviewer who can assess whether the contracting authority's decision-making was fair and transparent? This could provide assurance that the procurement process has been conducted in accordance with best practices.

compliance_checks.reasoning: This scenario is qualitative (Step 2B) as it does not contain any explicit formula, sub-scores, or numbers. The core allegation is that the contracting authority failed to discharge its duty to give sufficiently clear reasons for its evaluation decision. I will assess compliance qualitatively instead of quantitatively.

This scenario is qualitative, as it does not contain any explicit formula or numerical values. The core allegation is that the contracting authority failed to provide clear reasons for its evaluation decision, rather than a specific calculation being wrong. I will assess compliance qualitatively instead of performing a numeric computation.

applicable_provisions: Regulation 86(1) of the Public Contracts Regulations 2015
compliance_checks.reasoning: This scenario is qualitative, not numeric. The core allegation is that the contracting authority failed to discharge its duty to give sufficiently clear reasons for its evaluation decision. I do not need to perform a calculation here. However, I note that neither party has provided any specific numbers or scores that could be used to verify their claims. Based on my independent assessment, it appears that the contracting authority's failure to provide clear reasons for the scores awarded is a compliance issue. The parties' proposals for addressing this issue (additional training and revising procurement documentation vs. engaging an independent reviewer) do not directly address the lack of clear reasons provided.

ca_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: We have managed to avoid a lengthy and costly court battle, which would have likely taken 6-12 months and cost over £50k. This outcome is more favorable than our BATNA.
ca_win_statement.win_statement: We were able to negotiate a re-evaluation of the contract award, which addresses the claimants' concerns about transparency without having to resort to an external review or court proceedings.
what_was_achieved: Provided additional information on evaluation methodology and scoring breakdown
Offered compromise on independent review by neutral third-party expert
what_was_conceded: Agreed to consider an independent review of the evaluation process
Will provide additional training to evaluators on providing clear and transparent scoring reasons

bidder_win_statement.outcome_relative_to_batna: The final outcome of re-evaluation is better than our BATNA (pursuing damages or formal TCC proceedings), which would have been costly, slow, and uncertain. While we did not achieve a complete resolution to our concerns about the lack of clear reasons provided for the scores awarded, the contracting authority's willingness to consider an independent review by a neutral third-party expert is a step in the right direction.
bidder_win_statement.win_statement: We successfully negotiated a compromise that includes consideration for an independent review of the evaluation process, which will provide assurance that the procurement process has been conducted in accordance with best practices. This outcome acknowledges our concerns about transparency and provides a more satisfactory resolution than pursuing damages or formal TCC proceedings.
what_was_achieved: The contracting authority agreed to consider an independent review of the evaluation process by a neutral third-party expert
Additional training for evaluators on providing clear and transparent scoring reasons will be provided
what_was_conceded: We did not achieve our initial proposal for an external review, but instead had to compromise on internal measures
The contracting authority's willingness to revise procurement documentation is not as comprehensive as we would have liked

key_sticking_points: Lack of clear reasons provided for scores awarded
summary.concessions_summary: The Contracting Authority offered to provide additional information on their evaluation methodology and a detailed breakdown of how they applied the published criteria in this procurement. They also agreed to consider an independent review of their evaluation process by a neutral third-party expert. The Aggrieved Bidder proposed engaging an independent reviewer, but ultimately accepted the Contracting Authority's compromise of revising procurement documentation.
summary.court_reasoning_summary: The Court assessed each round qualitatively, focusing on whether the Contracting Authority discharged its duty to provide clear reasons for their evaluation decision. In Round 3, the Court determined that the Contracting Authority failed to comply with this duty and recommended re-evaluation.
summary.likely_next_steps: Re-evaluation of the procurement process is likely to occur, as recommended by the Court. This may involve revisiting the scoring and providing clear reasons for each score awarded.
summary.plain_english_summary: The dispute centered on the Contracting Authority's failure to provide clear reasons for their evaluation decision. The parties proposed different solutions, but ultimately, the Court determined that re-evaluation was necessary to ensure transparency and fairness in the procurement process.
